implementation.resident_air_buffers: each AIR runner allocates its query tiles, K/V and two output slots once as XRT buffer objects mapped as BF16 tensors; Q/K/V preparation writes into them directly; about 56 MB (self4096) and 28 MB (cross) replace the 40 MB and 12 MB sequential buffer sets, which are released
implementation.launch_api: start(tile, slot, upload_kv) syncs K/V (first tile only) and the query tile and launches without waiting; finish waits and syncs the output slot back
implementation.schedule: after the tiled QKV phase the NPU order per block is air0, air1, out0, air2, out1, air3, out2, out3; each finished AIR tile is quantized behind the next job before its output slot is reused; each out job's gated residual runs behind the next job; one NPU job in flight
implementation.error_handling: if host work fails mid-schedule, the job in flight is waited for before the error propagates
implementation.finiteness: the overlapped path skips AIR's separate finiteness passes: the fused Q/K/V preparation rejects nonfinite Q/K/V and the head-major quantization rejects nonfinite AIR output; the verified first prompt and 512x512 keep the sequential AIR call with its checks
implementation.overlap_gate: unchanged: ANIMA_XDNA_INT8_OVERLAP (default 1; 0 disables), tiled blocks only, after the four verified forwards

configuration.process_model: fresh standalone ComfyUI Python process per variant (real nodes, no HTTP server); the first run of every process includes the four verified forwards; the previous commit was re-measured in the same session from an export of that commit

concurrency_probe_ms.conclusion: the NPU does not run two hardware contexts concurrently to any useful degree; keep one job in flight and hide host work

runs.cold_run_note: every process this session, including the previous commit, ran the cold first prompt 2-5 s slower than the previous section, so the shift is machine state; the first prompt runs mostly the sequential verified path

previous_overlap.runs: previous section runs 1 and 2, then the re-measured run 1

exposed_npu_wait_seconds_per_warm_prompt.note: output projections expose more wait because less host work sits behind each out job; net attention saving about 2-4 s per prompt

regression_512.note: the 1024-token path does not use the overlapped schedule

limits: one machine, seed and prompt; one to three warm runs per variant
no CFG > 1, LoRA or HTTP/UI measurement
warm times of the same code varied by up to 2.1 s between runs and processes
not tried: per-block cross-attention K/V caching; fewer per-tile buffer syncs
